root_cause.text: The virtbt_rx_handle() function in the virtio_bt driver forwards received packets to hci_recv_frame() without validating that the remaining payload (after stripping the pkt_type byte) meets the minimum fixed HCI header length for the given packet type, allowing a truncated or zero-length skb to cause an out-of-bounds read of uninitialized buffer data when the core Bluetooth subsystem dereferences the header fields.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that "virtbt_rx_handle() reads the leading pkt_type byte from the RX skb and forwards the remainder to hci_recv_frame() for every event/ACL/SCO/ISO type, without checking that the remaining payload is at least the fixed HCI header for that type." It further explains that a one-byte completion (skb->len already pulled to 0) reaches hci_recv_frame(), and if the byte is HCI_ACLDATA_PKT, the fast-path in hci_dev_classify_pkt_type() dereferences hci_acl_hdr(skb)->handle, reading two bytes of uninitialized RX-buffer data. The patch adds a length check after a switch statement, requiring skb->len to be at least min_hdr (2 for event, 4 for ACL, 3 for SCO, 4 for ISO) before calling hci_recv_frame().

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a variable to store minimum header size for packet validation in virtbt_rx_handle, providing a guard against undersized packets.
intent_record.what: Added a local variable declaration 'size_t min_hdr;' inside virtbt_rx_handle, before the existing 'pkt_type' variable.
intent_record.how: The new variable min_hdr is declared to store a minimum header size value, which will likely be used later in the function to validate that the incoming sk_buff has sufficient length before processing the packet type. This prevents potential out-of-bounds access or processing of malformed packets.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add header length validation to virtbt_rx_handle to guard against undersized packets.
intent_record.what: Refactored the switch statement in virtbt_rx_handle to set a min_hdr variable per packet type, moved the common packet processing (hci_skb_pkt_type and hci_recv_frame) after a new length check, and changed the default case to return instead of break.
intent_record.how: Before processing a received packet, the code now checks if the skb length is at least the minimum header size for the packet type. If not, the packet is dropped with an error log. This prevents the Bluetooth stack from receiving malformed or truncated packets.

bic_trace_step.reason: In virtbt_rx_handle(), after reading pkt_type and pulling 1 byte, the function passes the skb to hci_recv_frame() for all handled packet types without checking that the remaining skb->len meets the minimum HCI header length for that type (e.g., HCI_EVENT_PKT requires at least 2 bytes after type, HCI_ACLDATA_PKT requires 4 bytes, etc.). This missing validation allows a truncated or zero-length skb to reach the core Bluetooth stack, potentially causing an out-of-bounds read of uninitialized buffer data.
